analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md only (head lines 605-1058). They are documentation and contain no code, config or auth logic, so no security behavior changed in these units. No finding qualifies on this evidence. The changelog describes security-relevant behavior implemented in other files, which I could not see. Later passes should check that the code matches these claims.

Claims to verify against code:
- 605-619, v0.9.9 App Attest: retire failed one-time enrollment keys with persistent generation budgets, and retry only serverUnavailable with the same key. Reprobe on a 1/5/10-minute backoff. A first grant still needs a fresh assertion and a verified risk receipt. Related threats: T-053, T-054, T-055, T-057, TB-011.
- 610 and 614: accept macOS CDhash attestation extensions when Apple omits the extension flag, only after chain, nonce and ACL verification. Also accept a fully signed, measured assertion. Check that arbitrary unflagged tails still fail. Related: T-054, TB-011.
- 614: recover serving authorization after a fresh, fully archived proof despite an earlier frame refusal. Check that this cannot bypass revocation or the final-handoff gate (T-053).
- 616: a 20-byte CandidateCDHash must match uniquely against one durably qualified full 32-byte hash. This should include revocation rows and exclude environment-only mappings (T-054, A-017).
- 613: private-only providers are excluded from the unauthenticated attestation roster and its shared cache. Public legacy SE keys remain linkable (T-058, TB-009).
- 612: public network counts show source snapshots, while owner serving controls keep live expiry. Historical display must never become authorization.
- 651-652 and 686-692: durable qualification and revocation fencing, bounded refresh, and blocking unqualified releases before the updater/latest aliases advance (A-017, T-024, T-025).
- 688 and 697: macOS 27+ skips MDM enrollment, with removal gated on a decision received within 10 seconds (T-057).
- 676: the first-content SLA is scoped to selected accounts via an environment allowlist, a deployment configuration item.

No canonical threat-model update is required from this documentation change alone.
